procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Same-day slot. Two days of yellow eyes and a yellowish tinge to his skin. He has been studying for exams and skipping meals, not much sleep. Feels fine otherwise. No pain, no itching, urine and stool look normal. Sugars a little higher than usual with the odd eating, no lows. Same pattern as the spells GI has seen (Dubin-Johnson in 2021, then a Gilbert-type spell last May).

Meds: glargine 16 u qhs, lispro scale, valacyclovir prn. NKDA.

O: vitals as charted. Looks well. Scleral icterus. Abdomen soft, nontender, liver and spleen not enlarged.

A/P
Recurrent jaundice in known Gilbert and Dubin-Johnson syndromes, triggered by fasting and short sleep. Hepatic panel with fractionation and CBC today to make sure it looks like his usual. Regular meals even during exams - set alarms if needed, which also helps the diabetes. Expect it to clear in a few days; call if it lingers past 2 weeks or if he gets pain, dark urine or pale stool.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Bilirubin is 3.2, mostly the indirect kind, with normal liver enzymes and a normal blood count. Same picture GI saw last spring. Nothing to treat. Eat regularly and it should fade over the next several days.

documents.title: Re: Liver tests
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. Already looking less yellow today. Back to actual meals.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 03/07/2023

Type 1 diabetes since 05/2021. Steady control. Meter average stable, highest readings in late January during exams with irregular meals. No severe hypoglycemia. A1c today.

Glargine 16 units at bedtime and lispro sliding scale continued. Discussed exercise snacks for the spring soccer season. Return 4 to 6 months.

Allergies: NKDA.
Endocrinology

documents.title: Valacyclovir refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Out of refills on the valacyclovir. No cold sore right now, I just like to have it in the drawer.

documents.title: Refill sent
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Valacyclovir 500 mg BID prn renewed per PCP, 30 tabs with 2 refills. Pt notified via portal.

medications.sig: Take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain, no more than 6 tablets a day

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Indication: right lower quadrant pain.
Technique: axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after intravenous contrast, with coronal and sagittal reformats.
Findings: The appendix is dilated with wall enhancement and surrounding fat stranding. No appendicolith. No extraluminal gas, fluid collection or abscess. Liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys are normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. Lung bases clear. No acute osseous abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Acute uncomplicated appendicitis. No perforation or abscess.

documents.title: Operative report: laparoscopic appendectomy
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 07/13/2023
Preoperative diagnosis: acute appendicitis
Postoperative diagnosis: same, uncomplicated
Procedure: laparoscopic appendectomy
Anesthesia: general endotracheal
Findings: inflamed, nonperforated appendix; no abscess or purulent fluid.
Description: three-port technique with umbilical access. Mesoappendix divided with energy device, base secured with a stapler. Specimen retrieved in a bag. Ports closed, skin with absorbable suture and glue.
EBL minimal. No complications. Insulin managed per perioperative protocol with endocrinology input by phone.
Pathology: acute appendicitis.
Allergies: NKDA.

[Scanned 09/05/2023]

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 07/13/2023 via the emergency department
Discharged: 07/14/2023

24-year-old man with type 1 diabetes, Gilbert and Dubin-Johnson syndromes, who came in overnight with right lower quadrant pain. WBC 13.4. CT showed uncomplicated acute appendicitis. Taken for laparoscopic appendectomy the same morning without complication. Pathology: acute appendicitis.

Hospital course: tolerated diet by the evening of surgery, pain controlled on acetaminophen, walking. Glucose managed on his home basal insulin with correction lispro. Discharged postoperative day 1.

Discharge medications: home insulin glargine 16 units at bedtime and lispro sliding scale; valacyclovir as needed; acetaminophen 500 mg 1 to 2 tablets every 6 hours as needed.
Activity: no heavy lifting or contact sports for 2 weeks.
Follow-up: general surgery clinic in 1 week.
Allergies: NKDA.

[Received 09/05/2023 after second request]

documents.title: Had my appendix out
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just letting you know I had my appendix out last Thursday at the hospital. Went in at night with bad pain on the right side, they did a CT and took it out laparoscopically that morning. Home since Friday, feeling ok, only taking Tylenol. I see the surgeon this week.

documents.title: Re: Had my appendix out
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry you went through that, and glad it went smoothly. Keep an eye on your sugars while you're less active and eating less. We'll ask the hospital for the records. Let's do a short video check after you've seen the surgeon.

documents.title: General surgery postoperative visit
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GENERAL SURGERY CLINIC - POSTOPERATIVE VISIT
Date of visit: 07/21/2023

One week out from laparoscopic appendectomy for uncomplicated acute appendicitis. Recovering well. For the last two days the whites of his eyes have looked yellow to him. No abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; bowels normal; passing gas; eating well, appetite better than in the hospital. No fevers or chills, no dark urine or pale stools. Walks every day. A little tired. Using acetaminophen now and then.
Known Gilbert and Dubin-Johnson syndromes with previous yellow spells during exam periods in 2022 and early 2023. He mentions his father was once told of 'some liver enzyme issue' that was never treated.

Exam: afebrile. Scleral icterus, skin not jaundiced. Abdomen soft, nontender. Port sites healed, no erythema, no fluid collection.

Labs: total bilirubin 3.1 mg/dL, indirect 2.8, direct 0.3. AST, ALT and alkaline phosphatase normal. Hemoglobin and hematocrit normal.

Impression: normal recovery. Icterus is an unconjugated rise consistent with his Gilbert syndrome after surgery and reduced intake, not a surgical complication.
Plan: resume full activity including soccer after 2 weeks from surgery. No further surgical follow-up needed.

Allergies: NKDA.
General Surgery

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home, identity confirmed.

Follow-up after laparoscopic appendectomy 7/13 at the regional hospital. Surgeon's note received: normal recovery, eyes yellowed for a few days afterward with an unconjugated bilirubin rise that fit his Gilbert syndrome. Yellow gone now. Back to running, cleared for soccer next week. Done with acetaminophen. Sugars back to his usual.

Incisions look healed on camera.

A/P
- s/p laparoscopic appendectomy - surgical history updated. Still waiting on hospital discharge paperwork; front desk to re-request.
- T1DM, Gilbert/Dubin-Johnson - unchanged.
Physical next year; flu in the fall.

documents.title: Hospital records re-requested
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hospital records not received from first request (7/18). Called the medical records office, re-faxed signed release for 7/13-7/14 admission: discharge summary, op note, CT and path.

documents.title: Flu and COVID vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (quadrivalent) left deltoid and 2023-24 COVID vaccine right deltoid, both IM. No acute illness. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Reminded him a sore arm and tiredness for a day can bump sugars a little.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Diabetic eye exam report, outside optometry practice. Exam date 11/09/2023.
Acuity 20/20 each eye uncorrected. Dilated exam: optic nerves healthy, maculae flat, no hemorrhages, exudates or microaneurysms. No diabetic retinopathy OU.
Next dilated exam in one year.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 01/23/2024

Type 1 diabetes, 2.5 years. Appendectomy last July went smoothly. Busy term with a part-time job, more skipped lunches and evening highs. No severe lows. A1c today, a little above last year's.

No change: glargine 16 units at bedtime, lispro sliding scale with meals. Encouraged pre-bolusing and not skipping lunch. Return 6 months.

Allergies: NKDA.
Endocrinology

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can you renew the test strips and pen needles? Endo said to ask you since you sent them last time. Also low on valacyclovir.

documents.title: Refills sent
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Per PCP: test strips (4x/day testing), pen needles 32G 4 mm, and valacyclovir 500 mg BID prn renewed to his pharmacy. Insulin pens stay with endocrinology. Pt notified.

documents.title: Dermatology visit
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY NOTE
Date of visit: 05/22/2024

25-year-old man with recurrent HSV-1, type 1 diabetes and Gilbert syndrome that flares with stress. Three days of painful sores on the lips and inside the mouth, with a mild fever. A tingling feeling in the area came first, then the blisters. He has had this a number of times, mostly with stress or short sleep.

Meds: insulin glargine, insulin lispro, valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily as needed. NKDA.

Exam: grouped vesicles and shallow erosions limited to the perioral skin and the oral mucosa. No eye involvement. No lesions elsewhere.

Assessment: herpes simplex virus infection, recurrence of his known HSV-1, clinical diagnosis.
Plan: take his valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily as prescribed now; supportive care with fluids and soft foods. Return or call for any eye pain or redness, or if lesions spread.

Dermatology

documents.title: Saw dermatology
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI I saw dermatology yesterday, the cold sores this time went inside my mouth too and I had a low fever. They said it's my usual herpes and to take the valacyclovir. Eating is annoying but I'm ok. Sugars are running a bit high.

documents.title: Re: Saw dermatology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. Stay on top of fluids, and keep checking more often while you're sick - follow your endocrinology sick-day plan for the highs. If you can't keep fluids down or you see ketones, call us right away. Let me know if it isn't clearly better in a week.

documents.title: Prior authorization: insulin lispro
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy says the student plan changed preferred rapid-acting insulin. Endocrinology office handling the PA for lispro pens; pharmacy gave him a 7-day supply in the meantime. Pt aware. Nothing further needed from us.

documents.title: Rooming
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Physical. Med list reviewed: glargine 16 units at bedtime, lispro per sliding scale, valacyclovir prn. NKDA. PHQ-9 = 4. Requests flu and covid.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PHYSICAL

25 y/o, still finishing his degree part-time while working. Overall well.

Interval: dermatology in May for an HSV-1 flare that spread inside the mouth with a low fever - healed within about 10 days on his valacyclovir, nothing since. No yellow spells since the one after his appendectomy last summer. Endocrinology in January; says the A1c 'crept up a bit' with skipped lunches. Has had his eye exam reminder, says he'll go this winter.

Meds: as rooming. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, playing soccer again.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well-appearing. No icterus. Lips and oral mucosa clear. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur; lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed port scars, no organomegaly. Feet: intact skin, normal monofilament, pulses palpable. Mood normal.

A/P
1. HSV infection (May episode) - resolved. Recurrent HSV-1 continues with episodic valacyclovir.
2. T1DM - with endocrinology. A1c, microalbumin, CMP, CBC, lipids today. Eye exam this winter.
3. Gilbert / Dubin-Johnson - quiet.
4. Flu and 2024-25 covid given. PHQ-9 4, exams and work stress, coping fine.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs look fine. A1c is a touch higher than a couple of years ago but close to where endocrinology has you; they'll fine-tune. Kidneys and urine protein normal, cholesterol normal, blood counts normal. Bilirubin mildly up with normal enzymes, your usual.

documents.title: Insurance card
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt uploaded new student health plan card for spring term. Same plan, new member ID. Demographics updated, eligibility verified.
